intro: Mock paper. Answer every question in the spaces provided. Show your working: marks are given for method. The marks for each question are shown in brackets.

questions.a: A) 1.5 × 10⁻². 15 × 10⁻³ = 1.5 × 10⁻². 15 × 10⁻³ is equal but not in standard form.

questions.q: x = 4.6 to 1 decimal place. What is the upper bound?
questions.a: A) 4.65. Half of 0.1 above: 4.65. 4.69 is not the bound; 4.7 rounds to 4.7.

questions.q: £800 depreciates by 10% a year. What is it worth after 2 years?
Make x the subject of y = (x + 2)/x.
questions.a: A) x = 2/(y − 1). xy = x + 2, xy − x = 2, x(y − 1) = 2. 2/(1 − y) has the sign wrong.

questions.q: Solve x² = 5x.
questions.a: A) x = 0 or x = 5. x² − 5x = 0, x(x − 5) = 0. Dividing by x loses x = 0.

Extend : The mass of a hydrogen atom is 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. How many hydrogen atoms are in 1 kg? Give your answer in standard form to 3 s.f.

questions.a: a + 2b = 6 and a − 2b = 0, so a = 3, b = 1.5

questions.q: Extend : d = 245 km to the nearest 5 km and t = 3.5 h to the nearest 0.1 h. Find the upper bound of the average speed.
Stretch : Find the lower bound of the speed and use both bounds to give the speed to a suitable degree of accuracy.
questions.a: 242.5 ÷ 3.55 = 68.3; both bounds round to 70 km/h to 1 s.f., so 70 km/h

questions.q: Write the bounds of 250 g to the nearest 10 g.
questions.model: Nearest 10 g: half of 10 is 5. Lower bound 250 − 5 = 245 g; upper bound 250 + 5 = 255 g.
